text:
maria (AE): Acme POC stuck. They POSTed a single JSON with ~9k examples and got 413 Request Entity Too Large. Need help ASAP for Friday demo.
ellie (SE): Do we have exact content-length or sample shape?
maria (AE): They reported ~11MB body. Each example ~1k chars. They thought model's 32k token window means we can accept it as one request.
kai (runtime eng): Hosted ingress default is 8MB. Logs show: 
```
ingress: reject: body_size=11.8MB > max_body=8MB
http: 413 returned to acme-client
```
jordan (sales): Security note: customer forbids presigned external uploads, so pointer-to-public-s3 is out. They asked whether splitting into multiple requests will increase cost. Need a simple clear answer.
kai (runtime eng): Short answer: billing is per-token. If you split into N requests and re-send long system/instruction prompts each time, you will pay those tokens N times. If you avoid re-sending the same system tokens (use session/KV cache or an assemble-on-server approach), you can avoid duplicate cost. Also multiple calls increase RPC overhead and latency.
ellie (SE): Immediate options: 1) Client chunking + server-side stitch (SDK helper), 2) Internal pointer fetch (they host the blob in a place we can fetch without presign), 3) Temporary ingress increase scoped to their org for the POC. Which can we do quickly?
kai (runtime eng): I can request EngInfra to enable a temporary body limit bump to 16MB for acme-org for 3-7 days, but Security must approve. I'll file the ticket with logs and risk notes.
maria (AE): Can we get that by tomorrow EOD? Demo is Friday.
deploy-bot: ticket INC-2031 created: "temporary ingress increase for acme-org POC" assigned to eng-infra.
ellie (SE): Quick hack: gzip client payload; if compressed size < limit, it may pass, but ingress decompresses and still enforces decompressed limit, so unreliable. Better to do chunked upload.
jordan (sales): For customer-facing explanation: recommend single-call pointer approach for cost-efficiency, but clarify security prevents presigned externals. If they can host internally and give us read access from our data plane, pointer works.
kai (runtime eng): Long-term: recommend Dedicated or Private where we control ingress and can accept larger bodies, plus predictable performance and predictable pricing.
ellie (SE): I'll prepare a short doc with 3 options and sample chunking code (uploadChunks + assemble) and a cost comparison example showing token counts for single vs split calls.
maria (AE): Thanks. Looping security and acme. Please update thread when ticket progresses.
